issue_context.summary: Keyboard Manager mappings for Win+Left and Win+Right do not prevent Windows Snap; the shell action wins instead of Home/End.
known_information: Stable and Preview versions are both reported affected.
The mappings are Win+Left -> Home and Win+Right -> End.
No bug report ZIP is attached.
The issue links older shortcut-remap reports #17344, #35730, and #17596; #17596 remains open but describes a broader intermittent shortcut failure.
Current code routes OS-level remapping through HandleOSLevelShortcutRemapEvent and has dedicated OS-level remapping tests.
inferences: The original Win event may not be suppressed, or replacement injection may fail after a successful match.
Windows Snap handling may expose a timing or modifier-state race.
issue_context.analysis: A short trace can distinguish the three plausible boundaries cheaply; a speculative code change would risk breaking other OS-level remaps.
initial_investigation: Search found related historical reports, but no current issue proves the same Win+Arrow-specific mechanism.
OSLevelShortcutRemappingTests.cpp provides a focused existing test seam.

comment.body: The mapping details and Windows build are useful, and the linked historical reports show this is a known Keyboard Manager area. The remaining decision is whether the original Win+Arrow reaches Windows Snap because the shortcut is not matched, because suppression returns too late/false, or because Home/End injection fails. Please reproduce with the two mappings active and submit a fresh report using `/bugreport` immediately afterward; if possible, include whether Snap still occurs with Snap layouts temporarily disabled and whether a non-shell shortcut remap works.
